sections.html:
Edmonds is a Puget Sound waterfront city in southwest Snohomish County, about 15 miles north of Seattle. Its 42,748 residents (July 1, 2025) are older than most Puget Sound suburbs, and the count is close to the 42,853 of 2020. Almost one resident in four is 65 or older. Owners occupy 70.9 percent of homes, and 88.2 percent of people were in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is low.

Who sells, and why, follows from that profile. Common triggers include downsizing, an inherited house, a move toward family and a rental the owner wants out of. Each brings its own paperwork.

Housing measureEdmonds figure
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020-202470.9%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024$890,100
Median gross rent, 2020-2024$1,903
Median household income, 2020-2024$122,449

A sale at the median value would cross into the second tier of the state excise tax, covered below.

Hillside neighborhoods ring a downtown valley here, so where a house sits inside the city matters to buyers. Expect distinct pockets:

  • Downtown and the Bowl: a valley with views of Puget Sound and the Olympic Mountains, close to the beach, the fishing pier and the ferry dock.
  • Five Corners, Firdale, Perrinville, Seaview, Sherwood and Westgate: hillside neighborhoods, several with their own small commercial centers.
  • The State Route 99 corridor: the eastern commercial edge, home to the city's car dealerships.
  • Esperance: an unincorporated enclave in the southeast corner that has resisted annexation, so confirm whether an address is inside city limits.

Transportation is a selling point. The Washington State Ferries route runs to Kingston, the downtown station is served by Amtrak and Sounder, and Community Transit buses reach outlying areas. Only about 11.7 percent of residents work inside the city and about 11 percent commute to Seattle, so buyers ask about transit and drive times first.

When you write the listing, name the pocket and its walk to the beach, pier or ferry dock, and say plainly if the house is a short drive from the Bowl instead of in it. A buyer shopping Five Corners or Westgate wants different details than one eyeing a view lot near the water, and a clear description saves showings that go nowhere.

The City of Edmonds requires a business license for any business operating in the city, including property owners, and it places home rentals in the General Business License category. The fee is $186.87 to apply and $74.75 to renew each year. You apply through the state Business Licensing Service on the Department of Revenue website, and the city then asks for a floor plan and a supplemental questionnaire. Business Licensing can be reached at 425-775-2525.

If tenants live in the house you are selling, check that the license is current and share the lease terms with the buyer. For building questions, the Planning and Development Department is at 121 5th Ave N, phone 425-771-0220. The city runs a Pre-Approved DADU Plan Program for detached accessory dwelling units, but no plans are in the catalog yet, so any existing backyard unit should come with permit records. Counter hours since September 2, 2025 are Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m., closed Wednesdays, with phone and digital help weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Call to confirm hours before you go.

  • Gather permit and inspection records for additions, decks and converted space.
  • Keep the rental license, lease copies and security deposit ledger together for the buyer.
  • Ask the department how to confirm an unpermitted structure before it surprises a buyer's inspector.

Three routes cover most Edmonds situations, and the choice turns on condition, timeline and how much preparation you want to do.

  • A traditional listing: strong demand for views and walkable streets, but staging, showings and financing contingencies take time.
  • A direct sale to an investor or cash buyer: fits an older house, an estate or a rental with tenants, with few repair requests and a closing date you can move.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale: you keep the agent fee but carry the disclosure, negotiation and paperwork.

Selling an estate? Have the probate attorney confirm that the personal representative can sign before you take an offer. Whatever the route, judge offers by what lands in your hands after excise tax, liens and any mortgage payoff.

A completed disclosure statement is part of any Edmonds house sale. RCW 64.06.020 excuses it only when the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt. Plan to hand it over in five business days from mutual acceptance, unless both sides agree to a different schedule; the buyer then gets three business days to rescind. The form asks about title, water, sewer, structural issues and more, and it says to write NA rather than leave blanks.

The tax falls due on the sale date, which the Department of Revenue defines as the day the deed is signed before the notary, no matter when it is recorded. Miss the one-month mark and interest runs back to the sale date, at 6 percent for 2026. Hold on to your sale records for four years or more. The state can audit a sale and ask you to back up the price or an exemption.

The state tiers start at 1.1 percent and rise to 1.28 percent above $525,000, plus a local rate. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 shift the first tier to $551,000.

Property tax in Snohomish County is paid in two installments, April 30 and October 31. Under RCW 84.56.020 a statement should arrive by March 15. If you are selling, confirm the second half was paid. The next installment is due April 30.

The county treasurer tells owners with a mortgage escrow to read their escrow statements, because money collected at a refinance may sit until April or October before it reaches the treasurer. Mailed payments only need a postmark by the due date. A late residential parcel of four or fewer units owes 9 percent interest a year and no extra penalty. At the treasurer's office the excise tax counter keeps weekday hours of 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Edmonds
sections.html: Once you accept an offer, escrow opens and title work shows any unpaid tax or lien. You complete the disclosure statement, sign the deed and settle the excise tax with the county treasurer. For an inherited house, line up the probate paperwork first. For a rental, hand the buyer the lease copies and the license record. With a cash buyer there is no bank appraisal, so your documents and title work set the pace. That helps a downsizing owner who needs a firm date.

faqs.q: Is a business license required to rent out an Edmonds house?
faqs.a: Yes. Edmonds treats home rentals as a General Business License, with a $186.87 application fee and a $74.75 annual renewal, filed through the state Department of Revenue system. Call Edmonds Business Licensing at 425-775-2525.

faqs.q: When must an Edmonds seller deliver the disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Five business days from the day both sides accept, unless they agree to another schedule. After delivery the buyer can rescind for three business days, or waive the form.

faqs.q: When is the excise tax due on an Edmonds sale?
faqs.a: It is owed when the deed is signed, and goes to the county treasurer. If a month passes unpaid, interest is charged back to the sale date.
No. Esperance is an unincorporated area in the southeast corner, surrounded by Edmonds, that has resisted annexation. Ask the county which jurisdiction handles permits and taxes for the address.

faqs.q: Do I need records for a backyard unit before selling?
faqs.a: Yes. The city has no plans in its DADU catalog yet, so any existing backyard unit should come with permit and inspection records. Planning and Development at 425-771-0220 can help.
